scenes.say: What happens when your Python code runs into trouble? How do you make sure errors don't crash your program?

scenes.label: try/except
scenes.sub: Catch and handle errors so your app keeps running.
scenes.say: In Python, try and except let you catch errors and handle them, so your app can keep going instead of crashing.
You can make your own exceptions by creating a class that inherits from Exception. This helps you signal specific problems in your code.
Custom exceptions make your error handling clear, give you more control, and make debugging much easier.

scenes.question: Is catching all exceptions a good idea?
scenes.right: No, catch specific exceptions to avoid hiding bugs.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: should you catch every exception? No way. Catch only what you expect, or you might miss real bugs.
